messages:
incidents-bot: paging alert — increased 5xx rates (model: red-13b-v1, region: us-west-2). 90th latency up, OOM signals on 6 nodes, node restarts detected. Alert group: serving-runtime/cuda-errors.
anjali: acked — I'm oncall. grabbing logs + will coordinate. tagging @tyler for runtime folks.
tyler: on it. starting by pulling runtime logs and recent model artifacts. guessing warmup path failing.
mike: quick snapshot from the node where the first restart happened — see repeated entries: 
```
2026-03-15T02:12:03Z runtime ERROR model_loader.go:412 failed to unmarshal model package: unexpected EOF
2026-03-15T02:12:04Z runtime WARN compile_cache.go:88 nvrtc: kernel compile timeout after 30s
2026-03-15T02:12:05Z cuda ERROR driver: cudaErrorOutOfMemory: allocation failed on GPU0
2026-03-15T02:12:06Z containerd INFO containerd: container exited with code 137
```
tyler: that pattern matches a cascade: deserialize (unexpected EOF) -> compile retry -> nvrtc timeout -> OOM -> container OOM kill. probable artifact corruption + aggressive compile timeout.
sara: we should failover traffic to quantized variant (red-13b-q8) as interim. I can flip routing for high-priority customers. minimal disruption.
anjali: do it. also cordon the problematic nodes so no new loads try to warmup there. @ops-bot can you post runbook snippet for cordon/drain?
ops-bot: runbook ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-warmup-failures 
Suggested steps: 
1) cordon + drain offending nodes
2) switch routing to fallback variant for affected model
3) restart model-controller on nodes after artifact validation
Commands: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17-usw2
kubectl drain gpu-node-17-usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
# route change (example)
curl -X POST https://controlplane.api.redwood/v1/routing/update -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"model":"red-13b-v1","fallback":"red-13b-q8","scope":"us-west-2","priority":"high"}'
```
mike: I validated artifact checksums for two recent versions; one had a truncated tarball. checksum mismatch + retry logic in loader was subtle and returned EOF instead of failing fast.
jeez: we need to also ensure the artifact download path has retries and a size check before unpack.
tyler: cordon + drain done for gpu-node-17-usw2 and gpu-node-22-usw2. re-routing to red-13b-q8 now.
sara: routing API accepted the change and traffic is shifting. monitoring. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: automated mitigation applied: 15% of traffic rerouted to red-13b-q8; critical customers pinned to q8.
anjali: customer impact check — @mike can you run quick query on 5xx counts and affected customer ids? we need SLA exposure.
mike: query results: 12 customers saw >=1 5xx between 02:11:30Z and 02:29:25Z. peak error period ~18 min. two customers had sustained failures for ~10m and triggered internal SLA alerts. estimated p95 latency degraded for 3 customers due to routing switch (falling back to q8). will extract list and hand to CS.
anjali: thanks. @eve from CS — can you draft a short post for affected customers with ETA for root cause and mitigation? include that requests were retried and a small fraction may have seen degraded throughput.
eve: will do. draft: "We experienced an incident impacting model red-13b-v1 in us-west-2 causing intermittent 5xx and degraded responses for some customers. Traffic was rerouted to a quantized fallback (red-13b-q8). We are investigating artifact integrity and compile-time handling; follow-up with root cause and timeline by EOD."
ops-bot: note: detected nvrtc compile-timeouts at 30s default. increasing compile timeout to 90s for fallback might reduce retries but could increase tail latency. Recommend adding backoff + streaming compile metrics.
tyler: temporary change: bumped nvrtc timeout to 90s on the controller for warmup tasks for red-13b-v1. will monitor compilation success rate and memory pressure.
mike: after routing change + cordon, OOM events dropped to zero on those nodes, container restarts stopped. we've collected the corrupted artifact: sha256 mismatch, truncated size 0.8GB vs expected 1.9GB.
anjali: setting incident priority to P1 for postmortem. assigning action items now.
eve: CS notified affected customers at 02:45Z.
anjali: action items (assignments):
- tyler: add preflight artifact size + checksum validation in loader, with explicit fail and alert (due EOD+3).
- mike: implement retry + backoff on model package download, and change EOF handling to explicit error (due EOD+5).
- sara: add routing automations to default to quantized variants when warmup failures exceed threshold (due next sprint).
- ops-bot: add runbook step to validate nvrtc metrics and auto-increase compile timeout temporarily (ops review).
- eve: coordinate customer follow-ups and SLA notes (due in 2 hours).
ops-bot: created incident ticket: INC-20260315-1787659999, linked to runbook and metrics dashboard.
anjali: any blockers?
tyler: need a CI test that simulates truncated artifact on warmup; asking infra for a test harness.
mike: no blockers from my side. prepping PR for EOF -> explicit error handling.
anjali: good work team. I'll keep this thread open until we've got the postmortem doc. For now mitigation stands and traffic stable.
incidents-bot: Incident resolved — mitigation successful, majority traffic on fallback, nodes healthy. Closing alert group. Follow-up required: postmortem and automation.
eve: postmortem draft link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20260315-1787659999/postmortem (will add timeline + RCA).
anjali: thanks all. adding retrospective note: test artifact uploads in CI, enforce artifact size checks at upload time, and add canary warmup step before route promotion.
